# 'Doanh nghiệp nên quản lý AI Agent như một người lao động'

AI Agent có thể tự lập kế hoạch và thực hiện nhiệm vụ, có thể được doanh nghiệp quản lý, thử nghiệm, phn quyền và đánh giá như một nhn sự. [...] Ông Nguyễn Quang Minh, Giám đốc Trung tm Tư vấn và Đổi mới sáng tạo AI (AI Lab), FPT Smart Cloud, cho biết như trên tại sự kiện AI4VN 2026. Đề xuất được đưa ra khi AI ngày càng tham gia su vào hoạt động doanh nghiệp. [...] Ở giai đoạn hiện tại, AI đã tiến hóa từ công cụ suy luận, hỏi đáp trở thành những tác nhn có năng lực thực thi - được gọi là AI Agent. Khác với chatbot chủ yếu phản hồi từng cu hỏi, AI Agent có thể nhận một mục tiêu, lập kế hoạch, lựa chọn công cụ, thực hiện nhiều bước và điều chỉnh dựa trên kết quả. Chẳng hạn, thay vì chỉ soạn một nội dung theo yêu cầu, hệ thống có thể tiếp nhận nhiệm vụ, tìm dữ liệu trong phạm vi được cấp quyền, xử lý thông tin và chuyển kết quả cho người phụ trách kiểm tra.

items.title: 子どものころ、
items.summary:
子どものころ、
「大きくなったら何になりたい？」と聞かれて、
なんと答えていましたか。

ケーキ屋さん。お医者さん。電車の運転士。
ひと言で言えた、あの夢。
いまでも覚えている人は多いかもしれません。

今日11月10日は「技能の日」。
1970年、アジアで初めての技能五輪国際大会が東京で開かれ、
その開会式の日にちなんで定められた日です。

中国語では、「〇〇になりたい」を
我想当〇〇（wǒ xiǎng dāng）と言います。
我想当医生。お医者さんになりたい。
我想当老师。先生になりたい。

当（dāng）は、「その役を引き受ける」という感じの字です。
「なりたい」より少しだけ、
「やってみたい」に近い気がします。

子どもに同じことを聞くと、
「まだ決めてない」と返ってくることもあります。

つい、
「じゃあ、好きなことは？」と
答えを急がせたくなるけれど。

決まっていないのは、
まだ全部を選べる、ということだから。

大人になると、夢は「何になるか」より
「何をしていたいか」に変わっていきます。

子どもの「なりたい」も、
職業の名前というより、
「あの人みたいに、何かができる人になりたい」
なのかもしれません。

だから今夜は、聞き方を少し変えてみたい。
「何になりたい？」ではなく、
「何ができるようになりたい？」と。

答えが毎年変わっても、たぶんそれでいい。
変わるたびに、
その子が見ている世界が、少し広がっているから。

職業の中国語を、2枚目のカードにまとめました。
保存して、寝る前に親子で「我想当…」と言い合ってみてください。

子どものころの夢、ひと言で教えてください。

items.title: WHAT THE FUCK IS THIS GUY TRYING TO DO?
items.summary:
WHAT THE FUCK IS THIS GUY TRYING TO DO? 

→ A man in a bright blue suit is balancing horizontally over a rooftop wall

→ Directly below him sits a green glass bottle on top of a stack of concrete blocks

→ He carefully holds a glass plate above the bottle

→ He tries to position everything while keeping his body suspended over the wall

→ But things quickly go wrong

→ He loses his balance and crashes onto the rooftop

→ The plate falls to the ground

→ And the final shot reveals his absolutely ridiculous hairstyle and mustache

The sequence is what makes this AI video funny.

The absurd physical setup immediately grabs attention. You have no idea what the guy is attempting, but you want to see whether he actually pulls it off.

Generated here, one still of the door and the drop ->  https://t.co/I9DM3a2zqG

Then comes the inevitable crash.

And that final close-up makes the whole thing even more ridiculous.

This is exactly the kind of AI-generated comedy that works in short-form content.

Absurd physical challenges
Unexpected fails
Surreal comedy
Recurring characters
Viral social media clips
The interesting part is how easily AI video generation can turn a completely ridiculous idea into a short visual gag.
One character, one impossible situation, one unexpected payoff.
And you can keep creating new scenarios with the same character.
Would you watch a whole series of this guy's ridiculous attempts?

Make the opening hook more explosiveMake the action sequence more cinematic

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
